title: Being made to · even if
titleJp: したくなくても、させられる
canDo: I can build the causative-passive of any verb by stacking causative + passive: 食べさせられる, 飲まされる, 話させられる, させられる, 来させられる.
I can tell about something I was made to do, with the person who was made to do it marked by は and the person who made them marked by に: 私は母に野菜を食べさせられました。
I can choose between 〜させられました (I was made to, and I didn't want to) and 〜させてくれました (they let me, and I wanted to).
I can say "even if…" with 〜ても on verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives and nouns: 雨がふっても, 高くても, ひまでも, 子どもでも.
I can keep the past tense only at the end of a sentence with ても: いくら待っても、バスは来ませんでした。

blocks.t: Warm-up: say aloud the causative (lesson 22-1) and the passive (lesson 21-1) of 食べる, 飲む, する and くる
Vocabulary: tap 🔊 on each word in block 3 and repeat it twice
Grammar: point a (causative-passive), with the stacking table in your notebook and one 🔬
Grammar: point b (〜ても), with the examples read aloud and one 🔬
Block 6: the Lesson 23 video or the Sakubi sections, only the part on the causative-passive and 〜ても, as a second explanation (read to understand, not to memorize)
Notebook homework + checking it against the answer key
Checklist (block 10) + write your questions in the lesson notebook

skills: Forming the causative (lesson 22-1): 食べさせる, 飲ませる, 話させる, させる, 来させる. It is the bottom layer of the causative-passive.
Forming the passive of る-verbs (lesson 21-1): drop the る and add られる. It is the top layer.
Making the て-form of verbs and adjectives (lessons 06-1 and 07-2), which is the base of 〜ても.
Remembering 〜てもいいです (lesson 06-3) and 〜なくてもいいです (lesson 17-2): this lesson's ても was already hidden inside them.

grammar.title: The causative-passive: 〜させられる
grammar.gloss: being made to do something (against your will)
grammar.explanation:
In lesson 22-1, the causative told the scene from the side of **the person giving the orders**: 母は私に野菜を食べさせました ("my mother made me eat vegetables"). The causative-passive tells the same scene from the side of **the person who was made to do it**: 私は母に野菜を食べさせられました ("I was made to eat vegetables by my mother"). It almost always carries a tone of **"I didn't want to"**. It works like English "I was made to…".

**A quick test: who actually does the action?** 書かせる — the topic makes **someone else** write. 書かれる — the topic is what gets written, or the one bothered by it: not the writer either. 書かせられる — the topic **is** the writer again, but not by choice: they were made to write.

**How to build it: stack two forms you already know.** First comes the causative (lesson 22-1). It always ends in 〜せる / 〜させる, so it conjugates like a る-verb. Then, on top of it, comes the passive of る-verbs (lesson 21-1): drop the る and add **られる**.
• る-verb: 食べる → 食べさせる → 食べさ**せられる**. Standard Japanese has no short form here.
• う-verb: 飲む → 飲ませる → 飲ま**せられる**. In speech, most う-verbs use a **short form**, where せら shrinks to さ: 飲ま**される**. Both are correct, and the short one is the more common in everyday speech: 待たされる, 歌わされる, 書かされる.
• う-verb ending in す: 話す → 話させる → 話さ**せられる**. Here the short form is **not** used (話さされる ✗), because it would give さ + さ.
• する → させる → **させられる**.
• くる → こさせる → **こさせられる** (来させられる).

**The sentence, block by block.** [the person made to do it]は | [the person who made them]に | [object]を | 〜させられました。 The PREDICATE (〜させられました) says "I was made to…"; the block with に is the person who gave the order. That person can stay unsaid: パーティーでビールを飲まされました ("At the party, I was made to drink beer").
• The result conjugates like any る-verb: させられます, させられた, させられて, させられない.
• You will also meet 考えさせられる ("it made me think"), about a film or a book that leaves you thinking. Here nobody is giving orders: the work itself makes you think.
• Going further (Sakubi): the short form comes from the spoken short causative you met in lesson 22-1 (書かす, 待たす). Put that す-verb into the passive, like any う-verb ending in す (話す → 話される), and you get 書かされる, 待たされる.
grammar.structure: [person made to do it] は [person who made them] に [object] を 〜させられる。 · 食べさせられる · 飲まされる (飲ませられる) · 話させられる · させられる · 来させられる

examples.jp: 子どものとき、母に毎日ピアノのれんしゅうをさせられました。
examples.kana: こどものとき、ははにまいにちピアノのれんしゅうをさせられました。
examples.romaji: Kodomo no toki, haha ni mainichi piano no renshū o saseraremashita.
examples.en: When I was a child, my mother made me practice the piano every day. [lit. as a child, I was made by my mother to do piano practice every day]

examples.jp: きのうのパーティーで、ペドロさんはみんなに歌を歌わされました。
examples.kana: きのうのパーティーで、ペドロさんはみんなにうたをうたわされました。
examples.romaji: Kinō no pātī de, Pedoro-san wa minna ni uta o utawasaremashita.
examples.en: At yesterday's party, Pedro was made to sing a song by everyone.

examples.jp: 駅でマリアさんに一時間待たされました。
examples.kana: えきでマリアさんにいちじかんまたされました。
examples.romaji: Eki de Maria-san ni ichijikan matasaremashita.
examples.en: At the station, Maria kept me waiting for an hour. [lit. I was made to wait an hour by Maria]

pitfalls: Don't confuse it with the plain passive (lesson 21-1). 食べられました = "it was eaten" or "someone ate (my)…"; 食べさせられました = "I was made to eat". The させ in the middle changes everything.

Don't swap the roles: the person who was made to do it takes は, and the person who made them takes に. 母は私に野菜を食べさせられました ✗ means that YOU made your mother eat vegetables → 私は母に野菜を食べさせられました ✓. If the は block is the person giving the orders, use the plain causative: 母は私に野菜を食べさせました ✓.
The stacking order is always causative → passive: 食べられさせる ✗ → 食べさせられる ✓. And verbs ending in す don't shorten: 話さされる ✗ → 話させられる ✓.

If you wanted to do it, don't use the causative-passive. "The manager let me go home early" (and you were glad): 早く帰らされました ✗ → 早く帰らせてくれました ✓ (lesson 22-1). 早く帰らされました sounds like "they sent me home early", against your will.
howToStudy: In your notebook, make a table with 3 columns (dictionary form → causative → causative-passive) for 8 verbs: 食べる, 飲む, 待つ, 歌う, 書く, 話す, する, くる. For the う-verbs, write both forms (long and short), except for 話す.

Tap 🔬 on example 1. 母に shows up as TARGET (here, the person who made you do it), ピアノのれんしゅうを as OBJECT and させられました as the PREDICATE. Read the predicate first ("I was made to do"), then ask: do what? (ピアノのれんしゅう) Who made me? (母)
Say aloud 3 things you were made to do as a child: 子どものとき、〜に〜させられました。 Record yourself and check that に is on the person who gave the orders.
grammar.flag: Check in your Genki II that this lesson has these points in this order.

grammar.title: 〜ても: even if…
grammar.gloss: the condition doesn't change the result
grammar.explanation:
〜ても says that **the condition doesn't change the result**: "even if X, Y". You already know this ても: it is inside 〜てもいいです (lesson 06-3, literally "even if you do it, it's fine") and 〜なくてもいいです (lesson 17-2).

**How to build it: て-form + も.** It really is the て-form plus も ("also, even"): the result stays true **even with** the condition.
• Verb: ふって → 雨がふっ**ても** ("even if it rains"). In the negative, 〜ない becomes 〜な**くても**, like an い-adjective: 分からなくても ("even if you don't understand").
• い-adjective: drop the い and add **くても** → 高くても. いい becomes **よくても**.
• な-adjective and noun: **でも**, without だ → ひまでも, 子どもでも.

**The sentence, block by block.** [condition 〜ても]、| [result]。 The PREDICATE is the result, at the end: it says what happens no matter what. The block with ても is only the condition that **can't** change that result.
• The tense (present or past) goes only at the end of the sentence. The ても form has no past: いくら待っても、バスは来ませんでした ("no matter how long I waited, the bus didn't come").
• With a question word, it becomes "no matter…": 何を食べても ("no matter what you eat"), どこに行っても ("wherever you go"), いくら勉強しても ("no matter how much you study").
• Going further (Sakubi): watch out for the other でも. At the start of a sentence, でも means "but" (でも、行きます。 = But I'll go.); after a question word, it means "any… at all" (なんでもいいです, lesson 10-3). Only a noun or な-adjective + でも is this lesson's "even if".
grammar.structure: [verb-て]も · [い-adj without い]くても · [な-adj / N]でも 、[result]。

examples.jp: あした雨がふっても、海に行きます。
examples.kana: あしたあめがふっても、うみにいきます。
examples.romaji: Ashita ame ga futte mo, umi ni ikimasu.
examples.en: Even if it rains tomorrow, I'll go to the beach.

examples.jp: この本は高くても、買いたいです。
examples.kana: このほんはたかくても、かいたいです。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa takakute mo, kaitai desu.
examples.en: Even if this book is expensive, I want to buy it.

examples.jp: 日本語が下手でも、毎日話したほうがいいですよ。
examples.kana: にほんごがへたでも、まいにちはなしたほうがいいですよ。
examples.romaji: Nihongo ga heta demo, mainichi hanashita hō ga ii desu yo.
examples.en: Even if your Japanese is poor, it's better to speak it every day.

pitfalls: The ても form has no past: 待ったても ✗. The past goes only at the end: いくら待っても、来ませんでした ✓.
い-adjectives lose the い: 高いても ✗ → 高くても ✓. And いい is irregular: いくても ✗ → よくても ✓. Negatives work the same way: 分からなかっても ✗ → 分からなくても ✓ (you may see なかっても online, but it isn't standard).
な-adjectives and nouns use でも, without だ: ひまだても ✗ → ひまでも ✓; 子どもだても ✗ → 子どもでも ✓.

ても × たら × のに. 雨がふったら、行きません = "if it rains, I won't go" (the rain changes the plan, lesson 17-2). For "even if it rains, I'll go" (nothing changes): 雨がふったら、行きます ✗ → 雨がふっても、行きます ✓. And のに (lesson 22-2) is closer to English "even though": it is about something that already happened, with surprise or frustration: 雨がふっているのに、出かけました ("even though it was raining, they went out").
howToStudy: In your notebook, make a table with 4 rows (verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, noun) and write 2 examples of 〜ても in each row. Include よくても and 分からなくても.

Tap 🔬 on example 3. 下手でも shows up as IF / WHEN (the condition), 話したほうが as SUBJECT and いいですよ as the PREDICATE. Read the predicate first ("it's better"), then ask: what is better? (speaking every day) And the condition that changes nothing? (even if your Japanese is poor)
Say aloud 3 promises of your own with ても: いそがしくても、毎日日本語を勉強します。 / つかれていても、〜。 / 雨がふっても、〜。

homework.intro: Do it by hand in your notebook, with the kanji you know and kana for the rest. Only then open the answer key, item by item, and check the readings too. Circle what you got wrong and redo it the next day. If you have the Genki II Workbook, do this lesson's exercises too.

tasks.prompt: Stack the forms: write the causative and then the causative-passive. For う-verbs (except those ending in す), give the short form too.

a.jp: 食べさせる → 食べさせられる
a.kana: たべさせる → たべさせられる

a.jp: 飲ませる → 飲ませられる／飲まされる
a.kana: のませる → のませられる／のまされる

items.note: う-verb: the short form (飲ま + される) is the most common one in speech.

a.jp: 待たせる → 待たせられる／待たされる
a.kana: またせる → またせられる／またされる

a.jp: 話させる → 話させられる
a.kana: はなさせる → はなさせられる

items.note: Ends in す: the short form is not used (話さされる ✗).

a.jp: させる → させられる

items.note: Irregular, but it follows the same stacking: させる + られる.

a.jp: 来させる → 来させられる
a.kana: こさせる → こさせられる

items.note: Here 来 is read こ.

tasks.prompt: Tell the same scene from the side of the person who was made to do it: change the causative into the causative-passive. The person who obeys goes to は, and the person who gives the order goes to に.

items.q: 先生は学生に作文を書かせました。

a.jp: 学生は先生に作文を書かされました。
a.kana: がくせいはせんせいにさくぶんをかかされました。
a.romaji: Gakusei wa sensei ni sakubun o kakasaremashita.

items.note: 書かせられました is also correct.

items.q: 店長はアルバイトの人にトイレのそうじをさせました。

a.jp: アルバイトの人は店長にトイレのそうじをさせられました。
a.kana: アルバイトのひとはてんちょうにトイレのそうじをさせられました。
a.romaji: Arubaito no hito wa tenchō ni toire no sōji o saseraremashita.

items.q: 友だちは私を三十分待たせました。

a.jp: 私は友だちに三十分待たされました。
a.kana: わたしはともだちにさんじゅっぷんまたされました。
a.romaji: Watashi wa tomodachi ni sanjuppun matasaremashita.

items.note: In the causative of 待つ, the person who waits usually takes を. In the causative-passive, the person who waited goes to は, and the person who kept them waiting goes to に.

items.q: 父は弟に野菜を食べさせました。

a.jp: 弟は父に野菜を食べさせられました。
a.kana: おとうとはちちにやさいをたべさせられました。
a.romaji: Otōto wa chichi ni yasai o tabesaseraremashita.

items.note: The object (野菜を) keeps its place and its particle.

tasks.prompt: Fill in the ても form of the word in parentheses. Before you write, decide: is it a verb, an い-adjective, a な-adjective or a noun?

items.q: （いそがしい）＿＿、毎日日本語を勉強します。

a.jp: いそがしくても、毎日日本語を勉強します。
a.kana: いそがしくても、まいにちにほんごをべんきょうします。
a.romaji: Isogashikute mo, mainichi nihongo o benkyō shimasu.

items.note: い-adjective: drop the い and add くても.

items.q: 天気が（いい）＿＿、今日は出かけません。

a.jp: 天気がよくても、今日は出かけません。
a.kana: てんきがよくても、きょうはでかけません。
a.romaji: Tenki ga yokute mo, kyō wa dekakemasen.

items.note: いい is irregular: よくても.

items.q: 父は（日曜日）＿＿、会社に行きます。

a.jp: 父は日曜日でも、会社に行きます。
a.kana: ちちはにちようびでも、かいしゃにいきます。
a.romaji: Chichi wa nichiyōbi demo, kaisha ni ikimasu.

items.q: （ひま）＿＿、ゲームはあまりしません。

a.jp: ひまでも、ゲームはあまりしません。
a.romaji: Hima demo, gēmu wa amari shimasen.

items.note: な-adjective: でも, just like a noun.

items.q: 意味が（分からない）＿＿、最後まで読んでください。

a.jp: 意味が分からなくても、最後まで読んでください。
a.kana: いみがわからなくても、さいごまでよんでください。
a.romaji: Imi ga wakaranakute mo, saigo made yonde kudasai.

items.note: Negative: 〜ない becomes 〜なくても, like an い-adjective.

items.q: あした（雪がふる）＿＿、学校は休みになりません。

a.jp: あした雪がふっても、学校は休みになりません。
a.kana: あしたゆきがふっても、がっこうはやすみになりません。
a.romaji: Ashita yuki ga futte mo, gakkō wa yasumi ni narimasen.

tasks.prompt: Write 4 sentences about yourself: 2 about things you were (or are) made to do, saying who made you, and 2 with 〜ても about something you do no matter what. Then read them aloud and record yourself on your phone.

items.q: Model (match its structure, not its words):

a.jp: 子どものとき、母に毎日部屋のそうじをさせられました。学校では、先生に漢字をたくさん書かされました。でも、いそがしくても、今は毎日日本語を勉強しています。つかれていても、ねる前に少し本を読みます。
a.kana: こどものとき、ははにまいにちへやのそうじをさせられました。がっこうでは、せんせいにかんじをたくさんかかされました。でも、いそがしくても、いまはまいにちにほんごをべんきょうしています。つかれていても、ねるまえにすこしほんをよみます。
a.romaji: Kodomo no toki, haha ni mainichi heya no sōji o saseraremashita. Gakkō de wa, sensei ni kanji o takusan kakasaremashita. Demo, isogashikute mo, ima wa mainichi nihongo o benkyō shite imasu. Tsukarete ite mo, neru mae ni sukoshi hon o yomimasu.
a.en: When I was a child, my mother made me clean my room every day. At school, the teacher made me write lots of kanji. But now, even when I'm busy, I study Japanese every day. Even when I'm tired, I read a little before I go to bed.

items.note: Check: the person who gave the orders takes に, the causative-passive comes at the end (させられました, 書かされました), い-adjectives take くても, and the past tense appears only in the predicate.

practice.what: Play in the N4 areas and levels. Whenever a line of dialogue has 〜させられる (or a short form like 待たされる) or 〜ても, pause and answer out loud: who made whom do what? Or: which condition doesn't change the result? Copy 2 of those lines into your notebook and underline the predicate. Log the session in Immersion → Games and save the clearest line with ⛏ Mining (mark one new word and fill it in with the 📖 Dictionary button).

Drills → 🔬 Anatomy → 🔬 Analyze: paste the 3 causative-passive examples and check which block is the PREDICATE and which one holds the person who made you do it (the に block, shown as TARGET). Then paste 先生は学生に作文を書かせました and 学生は先生に作文を書かされました: the same blocks, but the TOPIC and the TARGET have swapped people. Last, vocabulary: the Genki II words are not a ready-made deck in the app, so add the words from block 3 you don't know yet (野菜, 下手, 意味, 最後…) with ⛏ Mining, each inside a sentence from this lesson. Learn the kanji inside the words (野菜, 意味, 最後), not one by one: a reading sticks best inside a word you use.

Try an easy manga, the classic first step into native reading (for example よつばと!, in a copy you buy or borrow): read a few pages for fun, looking up only the words that block the story. Characters complain a lot, so hunt for 〜ても and for 〜される / 〜させられる, and save one line you understood with ⛏ Mining. Prefer something gentler? A story from Tadoku's free graded readers (Resources tab) works too.
Tap 🔊 on each example in this lesson and repeat along 3 times. させられました has 7 beats of the same length: さ・せ・ら・れ・ま・し・た.

Record 30 seconds telling 3 things you were made to do as a child and 1 thing you do even when you're tired (つかれていても、〜). Listen and check the に and the ても. Then type the same sentences into the Journal and open "Anatomy of what I wrote": the causative-passive should be the PREDICATE at the end, and the person who made you do it should show up as TARGET (with に).

culture.title: Farewell parties (そうべつかい)
culture.body: When someone leaves a group, whether for a new job, a transfer to another city (てんきん), retirement or graduation, the colleagues usually organize a **送別会 (そうべつかい)**, a farewell party. It is usually a dinner at a restaurant or an いざかや, and the guest of honor usually doesn't pay their share. At the end, it's common for them to receive flowers or a gift and give a short あいさつ (a few words of thanks), with phrases like いろいろお世話になりました。 Because the fiscal year and the school year start in April, March usually has a lot of 送別会, and April brings the welcome parties (かんげいかい).
culture.try: Prepare your own farewell あいさつ in 3 sentences: a funny memory with the causative-passive (最初の日に、〜させられました), a thank-you (いろいろお世話になりました) and a promise with ても (どこに行っても、〜).

checklist: I can build the causative-passive of 食べる, 飲む, 話す, する and くる without looking, and I know which verbs have the short form.
I can explain the stacking: causative (させる) + passive (られる) = させられる.
I can say who was made to do it (は) and who made them (に) without swapping the roles.
I know when NOT to use the causative-passive: if I wanted to do it, I use 〜させてくれました (lesson 22-1).
I can make 〜ても with verbs, い-adjectives (including よくても), な-adjectives and nouns (でも).
I keep the past tense only at the end of a sentence with ても.
I did the homework, checked it against the answer key and redid what I got wrong.
If I have the Genki II Workbook, I did the exercises for this part of Lesson 23.
